newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian flag carrier adds service to China.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian flag carrier adds service to China.

text.p: Royal Air Cambodge (RAC) will become the first Cambodian airline to fly to mainland China when it begins twice-weekly flights to southern Guangzhou next month, airline chairman Vichit Ith said.
The airline was also considering services to Jakarta, Manila and Rangoon, he said late on Wednesday as he launched a promotional campaign.

"We have increased our market share on each of our (international) destinations this year...ranging from 19 to 48.7 percent," Vichit Ith said, adding that the airline had made the biggest gains on its Hong Kong route.
RAC also flies to Bangkok, Ho Chi Minh City, Kuala Lumpur and Singapore and provides services to eight destinations in Cambodia.

Vichit Ith said the airline had launched a $300,000 trade advertising campaign to publicise its routes and take advantage of the nine percent growth in airline traffic in the intra-Asian market -- the highest rate in the world.
RAC began operating in January 1995. It is a joint venture between Malaysian Helicopter Services, the parent company of Malaysia Airlines, and the Cambodian government.
The airline lost $7 million last year but expects to halve that loss in 1996. It hoped to make a profit by 1997, Vichit Ith said.
RAC is expected to carry 500,000 passengers this year, up from 326,000 last year. It has a fleet of two Boeing 737-400s and three ATR-72s.
